covered_actors: Frontier developers (any person who has trained, or initiated training of, a foundation model trained using > 10^26 integer or floating-point operations including original training, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, or material modifications)
Large frontier developers (frontier developers that together with affiliates had annual gross revenues exceeding $500,000,000 in the preceding calendar year)
Covered employees (employees responsible for assessing, managing, or addressing risk of critical safety incidents) protected under Labor Code §§ 1107–1107.2
California Office of Emergency Services (CalOES), California Attorney General, California Department of Technology, and California Government Operations Agency (CalCompute consortium)
prohibited_practices: Making a materially false or misleading statement about catastrophic risk from frontier models or management of catastrophic risk (for frontier developers), or about implementation of or compliance with a frontier AI framework (for large frontier developers), excluding reasonable good-faith statements (Bus. & Prof. Code § 22757.12(e))

Adopting, enforcing, or entering into any rule, regulation, policy, or contract preventing a covered employee from disclosing—or retaliating against a covered employee for disclosing—reasonable-cause information that a frontier developer's activities pose a specific and substantial danger to public health or safety from catastrophic risk or violate the TFAIA (Labor Code § 1107.1(a)–(b))

(j) “Large frontier developer” means a frontier developer that together with its affiliates collectively had annual gross revenues in excess of five hundred million dollars ($500,000,000) in the preceding calendar year.

enforcement_authorities: California Attorney General (exclusive enforcement authority for TFAIA civil penalties up to $1,000,000 per violation; whistleblower report intake and annual reporting)
California Office of Emergency Services (CalOES) (critical safety incident and internal-use risk assessment intake, review, federal-equivalency regulations, and annual aggregated reporting)
California Department of Technology (annual review and legislative recommendations on frontier model and developer definitions)
California Government Operations Agency (CalCompute consortium framework report)
California Superior Courts (civil penalty actions by the Attorney General and injunctive relief and attorney's fees actions by whistleblowers under Labor Code § 1107.1)
Law enforcement and public safety agencies with jurisdiction (24-hour imminent-risk critical safety incident notifications)
compliance_deadlines: 2026-01-01: Effective date for TFAIA transparency, safety framework, incident reporting, and Labor Code whistleblower protections
Before or concurrently with deploying a new or substantially modified frontier model: Publish frontier model transparency report (Bus. & Prof. Code § 22757.12(c))
At least once per year: Review and update frontier AI framework (§ 22757.12(b)(1))
Within 30 days of material modification: Publish modified frontier AI framework and justification (§ 22757.12(b)(2))

Every 3 months (or developer-specified reasonable schedule): Transmit internal-use catastrophic-risk assessment summary to CalOES (§ 22757.12(d)); quarterly sharing of anonymous whistleblower reports with officers/directors (Labor Code § 1107.1(e)(2))

Within 15 days of discovering a critical safety incident (or within 24 hours if posing imminent risk of death or serious physical injury): Report to CalOES or appropriate public safety authority (§ 22757.13(c))
5 years: Retain unredacted versions of redacted published compliance documents (§ 22757.12(f)(2))

On or before 2027-01-01 (and annually thereafter for CalOES/DT/AG): CalCompute framework report to Legislature (subject to appropriation), Dept. of Technology threshold recommendations, and CalOES/AG annual aggregated reports
penalties_summary: A large frontier developer that fails to publish or transmit a required document, makes a materially false or misleading statement about catastrophic risk or framework compliance, fails to report a critical safety incident, or fails to comply with its own published frontier AI framework is subject to a civil penalty of up to $1,000,000 per violation depending on severity, recoverable exclusively in a civil action brought by the California Attorney General (Bus. & Prof. Code § 22757.15). Under Labor Code § 1107.1, covered-employee whistleblowers may seek temporary, preliminary, and permanent injunctive relief (not stayed pending appeal) and reasonable attorney's fees, with a burden-shifting standard requiring clear and convincing proof of an independent legitimate basis.
implementation_notes: Enacted September 29, 2025, effective January 1, 2026. Adds three distinct statutory pillars: (1) Bus. & Prof. Code §§ 22757.10–22757.16 (TFAIA), imposing a >10^26 FLOPs frontier model threshold and >$500M revenue large-frontier-developer tier, mandatory published frontier AI frameworks covering catastrophic-risk thresholds, mitigations, third-party assessments, and unreleased model-weight cybersecurity, pre-deployment transparency reports (satisfiable via model/system cards), quarterly confidential CalOES internal-use risk summaries, 15-day/24-hour critical safety incident reporting, and CalOES federal-equivalency compliance recognition; (2) Gov. Code § 11546.8 establishing a 14-member CalCompute public cloud cluster consortium (operative upon budget appropriation); and (3) Labor Code §§ 1107–1107.2 granting frontier AI safety whistleblower anti-retaliation protections and requiring anonymous internal reporting channels for large frontier developers. Preempts local California frontier catastrophic-risk regulations adopted on or after January 1, 2025.
